strongest_angle: Examination of the October 2026 European Cockpit Association survey revealing that nearly 24% of European airline pilots routinely fly while too fatigued, and three in four have experienced cockpit microsleeps.

key_facts.fact: According to a European Cockpit Association report published in October 2026, nearly a quarter of European airline pilots routinely fly despite being too fatigued to work.
The European Cockpit Association survey of almost 7,200 captains and first officers found that three in four European airline pilots have experienced microsleeps in the cockpit.
A survey conducted by the European Cockpit Association revealed that over half of participating pilots consider that fatigue risk is not well managed in their airline.
According to Euronews reporting from October 2026 on the European Cockpit Association survey, more than half of surveyed pilots admitted they flew while tired.
